title: All-Time Great Indian Thrillers
description: 25 masterfully crafted Indian films built around suspense, mystery, psychological tension, investigation and unforgettable twists.
intro: A thriller lives or dies on its final act. These made it out alive.

entries.why_it_ranks: Jeethu Joseph turns an ordinary family's attempt to conceal a crime into an extraordinary battle of intelligence, with one of Indian cinema's most satisfying payoffs.
Dark comedy, murder and unreliable perception combine in a screenplay that repeatedly changes what we think we know.
Vidya Balan's search through Kolkata develops into a beautifully controlled mystery with an exceptional climax.
One of India's most effective serial-killer thrillers, driven by investigation, escalating danger and an unforgettable antagonist.
A rare sequel that intelligently exploits everything established in the original and proves Georgekutty's story was far from finished.
A police officer investigating a murder while struggling with his own lost memory leads to one of Malayalam cinema's boldest revelations.
Minimal locations and two superb performers are enough to create relentless tension between Naseeruddin Shah's anonymous caller and Anupam Kher's police commissioner.
An exceptionally economical mystery where perspective, memory and apparently insignificant details continually alter the investigation.
A polished serial-killer procedural that combines forensic investigation, psychology and escalating tension extremely effectively.
A missing-child mystery in which even the existence of the missing girl is questioned, creating an excellent sense of paranoia.
A murder investigation gradually becomes a story about grief, guilt and the supernatural, with an unusually emotional resolution.
A woman discovers that an entire day has disappeared from her memory and must reconstruct what happened before the consequences catch up with her.
Pawan Kumar transforms a seemingly minor traffic-rule investigation into an increasingly disturbing mystery.
A murder investigation becomes extraordinarily complicated when police discover two apparently identical suspects.
One of Hindi cinema's finest neo-noir mysteries, using a small Rajasthan town to create an atmosphere of corruption, secrets and paranoia.
Every new version of events forces the audience to reconsider victim, perpetrator and motive.
Vishal Bhardwaj and Meghna Gulzar examine competing theories of a murder investigation without providing the audience easy certainty.
Prithviraj's troubled police officer follows an unusual pattern connecting a series of murders in a strong investigative thriller.
Sukumar uses memory, hallucination and childhood trauma to make both the protagonist and audience question what is actually real.
An excellent modern procedural built around two very different investigators pursuing a serial killer.
Amitabh Bachchan and Taapsee Pannu turn an extended interrogation into a constantly shifting battle over what really happened.
What initially appears to be a strange police complaint gradually reveals a much darker story, with nonlinear storytelling producing a powerful payoff.
A retired policeman's investigative instincts lead him toward a disturbing conspiracy while his own personal tragedy gives the mystery emotional weight.
Naveen Polishetty's eccentric detective brings humour and personality to a mystery that becomes considerably darker than its opening suggests.
Anurag Kashyap's surreal psychological thriller remains one of mainstream-adjacent Indian cinema's strangest explorations of control, addiction and paranoia.
